headline: Approved $749 payment for Ingersol property monitoring; had no comments on 2 Perkins Road subdivision.
summary: Discussion covered a lot line adjustment at 16 & 22 Delta Drive and a site visit for a property being considered for purchase. Trail work at the Mathes Trail and a beaver dam at Faucher Road also came up. Mike Speltz was appointed to vote for the seat left open by Harry Schwartz's resignation.
decisions: Approved paying $749 to RCCD for monitoring the Ingersol property, from the line item budget, unanimously.
Gave no comments to the Planning Board on the 2 Perkins Road subdivision.
Appointed Mike Speltz to vote for the position vacated by Harry Schwartz.
Approved the July 14, 2026 minutes as amended, with one abstention.
Agreed to schedule a site visit for a property being considered for purchase on Tuesday, August 18th at 1:00 p.m.
Agreed to maintain the Mathes trail without consulting NH Fish & Game, but to notify them before maintenance work.

decision_evidence.quote: G. Harrington moved to pay the annual estimate from RCCD for $749 for monitoring the Ingersol property out of the line item budget. B. Maxwell seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously.
DRC – 2 Perkins Road - Subdivision - Map 13 Lot 22 ... Commission Comments: The Commission had no comments for the Planning Board.
M. Badois appointed Mike Speltz to vote for the position vacated by Harry Schwartz.
B. Maxwell moved to accept the minutes of the July 14, 2026, meeting as amended. D. Heafey seconded the motion. The motion carried, with E. Bickford abstaining.
They agreed to schedule it on Tuesday, August 18th at 1:00 p.m.
The Commission agreed they were allowed to maintain the trail without consulting NHF&G, but would notify them that maintenance work was going to be done.

plain_text:
Londonderry Conservation Commission
Tuesday, August 11, 2026
Draft Minutes
1 Present: Marge Badois, Chair; Gene Harrington, Vice Chair; Bob Maxwell, member; David Heafey, 
2 member; Elkel Bickford, member; Michael Speltz, alternate member; Gary Della Grotta, alternate 
3 member; Susan Malouin, alternate member
4
5 Absent: Deb Lievens, member
6
7 Also present: Michael Bazegian, GIS Manager/Comprehensive Planner
8
9
10 Call to Order and Roll Call
11 Ms. Badois called the meeting to order at 7:30 p.m. She reported Harry Schwartz has resigned from the 
12 Commission, so there is a vacancy for a full member. Gary Della Grotta agreed to move into the full 
13 member position. His vacant alternate position will be posted. 
14
15 DRC – 16 & 22 Delta Drive - Lot Line Adjustment - Map 14 Lots 21-11 & 4
16 The applicant was not present.
17
18 The Commission questioned the reason for this proposed adjustment. B. Maxwell said it appeared from 
19 the application that someone would like to purchase the lot with the existing building, but does not 
20 want the additional land. The applicant proposed adjusting the lot line to reduce the size of that lot and 
21 increase the size of the other lot, which could make it more attractive to potential interested parties.
22
23 The Commission questioned whether, due to the location of the wetlands, a dredge and fill permit 
24 would be needed to access the lot once this portion is transferred. They determined the property could 
25 be accessed from the northeast corner off Delta Drive or from the cul-de-sac. They questioned how 
26 water transferred between the wetlands on the property. They also discussed a proposed temporary 
27 drainage easement on the property.
28
29 Commission Comments: This could create a future problem for the transferred acreage due to having to 
30 cross wetlands to access it. 
31
32 DRC – 2 Perkins Road - Subdivision - Map 13 Lot 22
33 The applicant was not present.
34
35 The Commission questioned the presence of heavy equipment on Perkins Road at the cut-in to the 
36 western parcel. They noted the steepness of the planned driveway to access the second lot. They said 
37 the wetlands are not big enough for a buffer. They agreed if the forest cover is left as shown on the plan,
38 it will provide noise mitigation. They mentioned possible traffic and site distance issues, which are not in
39 the Commission's purview. 
40
41 Commission Comments: The Commission had no comments for the Planning Board.
Londonderry Conservation Commission
Tuesday, August 11, 2026
Draft Minutes
42
43 Public Comment
44 There were no members of the public present.
45
46 Old Business
47
48 Recreation Plan
49 M. Badois attempted to contact the company responsible for creating the recreation plan, but had no 
50 success. She will continue to try.
51
52 Site Visit
53 M. Speltz suggested a site visit is needed for the property the Commission is considering purchasing. 
54 They agreed to schedule it on Tuesday, August 18th at 1:00 p.m.
55
56 Sign Design
57 M. Speltz reported the sign builders have completed the design.
58
59 New Business
60
61 Mathes Trail
62 M. Badois reported a mountain bike rider informed her that the Mathes trail is practically impassible. A 
63 power tool might be needed, such as a brush mower, to clear the trail. She suggested this work be done 
64 in the fall. She noted the entrance to the trail on Faucher Road has been mowed and believes Trailways 
65 is working on this. She will check with Trailways to see if work on these projects can be coordinated. 
66
67 M. Badois said the beaver dam at Faucher Road is two feet above the boardwalk. Tom Kimball reported 
68 the water is backing up into the Londonderry Country Club and requested that something be done. The 
69 Commission discussed how this issue was addressed in the past. M. Badois will speak to DPW about this.
70
71 M. Speltz noted New Hampshire Fish & Game owns the Mathes property and there is an MOU with 
72 them. The Commission agreed they were allowed to maintain the trail without consulting NHF&G, but 
73 would notify them that maintenance work was going to be done.
74
75 Map Updates
76 M. Badois asked Mr. Bazegian how many of the newer trails are on the trail map, as new maps need to 
77 be printed. She also asked how to make the trail map available online. She noted the need to ask Mike 
78 Byerly what color blazes he used on the Piper Rising trail. 
79
80 Forest Society
81 M. Badois and M. Speltz met with Ilissa Sargent from the Forest Society, and discussed that monitoring 
82 reports showing multiple encroachments have gone unanswered. M. Badois received a response from 
83
Londonderry Conservation Commission
Tuesday, August 11, 2026
Draft Minutes
84 the Forest Society: they have been corresponding with individuals about the encroachments, but nothing
85 has been done to remedy them. They did not inform the Commission that these actions had been taken. 
86
87 Taking Action for Wildlife
88 M. Badois reported Taking Action for Wildlife has a Community Technical Assistance Program that 
89 provides information on a variety of topics to conservation commissions. The Commission discussed 
90 whether any of the items identified on the strategic plan might be a good match.
91
92 M. Badois appointed Mike Speltz to vote for the position vacated by Harry Schwartz.
93
94 RCCD Monitoring - Ingersol
95
96 G. Harrington moved to pay the annual estimate from RCCD for $749 for monitoring the Ingersol 
97 property out of the line item budget. B. Maxwell seconded the motion. The motion carried
98 unanimously. 
99
100 Hickory Hill Kiosk
101 B. Maxwell reported the Hickory Hill kiosk is inaccessible. After the parking lot was put in, people 
102 stopped using the trail, so it is overgrown. M. Badois said the kiosk needs to be moved and the path 
103 stabilized. The parking lot and the trail that is currently being used need to be put on the map.
104
105 Gate at Cooper Parcel
106 M. Badois reported the gate where the power lines cross Litchfield Road was left open. She closed it, but
107 there is no lock. She will find out who to contact at Eversource about this.
108
109 Approval of Minutes
110 On line 51, change "They spoke against shelving the Master Plan" to "They spoke against drastically 
111 modifying the Master Plan." M. Speltz reported the Strategic Plan is being held in abeyance until next 
112 spring, when the process will begin again. 
113
114 B. Maxwell moved to accept the minutes of the July 14, 2026, meeting as amended. D. Heafey 
115 seconded the motion. The motion carried, with E. Bickford abstaining.
116
117 Adjournment
118
119 G. Harrington made a motion to adjourn. E. Bickford seconded the motion. The motion carried 
120 unanimously. 
121
122 The meeting was adjourned at 8:09 p.m.
123
124 Respectfully submitted, Beth Hanggeli, Recording Secretary
